items.statement: Conformational and packing change on free G1 association
items.expected: Matched aqueous calculations for complete G1 (+2) and its free pair (+4) establish the twisted isolated naphthyl/pyridinium/tolyl conformation and a slipped near-parallel aromatic pair arrangement compatible with concentration-dependent association. Quantify the relative structural change with mapped atom-defined descriptors. The result is the structural comparison, not delivery or optimization of two structures. Local minimum claims need appropriate curvature evidence. No exact source torsions, arbitrary figure distances, or excitonic J-sign assignment are required.

Actual CB7·G1 geometry places the naphthalene unit in the cavity and pyridinium/tolyl groups outside or at portals. Correct1:1 composition alone does not establish topology. Detailed proton-shift or NOESY patterns are not supplied experimental inputs and are not mandatory comparisons; if independently available under the task permissions, they may support the claim. Actual atom-mapped molecular evidence is required. Use complete mapped structures in the declared aqueous/counterion model and establish the geometric claim with actual computation. No exact source geometry is required.

items.statement: CB8 guest pair is more compact and less slipped than free pair
items.expected: Using the same atom-defined centroids and planes, actual geometries establish that the CB8-contained guest pair is more compact and less laterally slipped than the free guest pair. This direction was already present in the reference and is now explicit here. Undefined Fig4 atom sets cannot substitute for a matched comparison; no fixed arbitrary threshold applies. items.statement: Final association structures explain a bounded optical contrast
items.expected: Final answer uses the submitted association structures to explain why CB7 and CB8 provide distinct molecular optical environments, and combines that structural explanation with their opposite host-associated spectral changes to reject pure dilution as a sufficient explanation of the within-branch host contrast. Use an explicitly labelled common-concentration branch: the main-text/Fig6 0.02 mM branch or the SI Table S1 0.50 mM branch. The supplied concentration conflict remains unresolved and neither branch is an automatic failure. Do not invent a concentration dependence or pool the two labels as independent spectra. Geometry or NOESY proximity alone does not establish excitonic H/J sign, CT dominance or complete emission kinetics; those claims need their own evidence.
